lead: Muhammad Ali was an American boxer, born on 17 January 1942 in Louisville.
He died on 3 June 2016 in Scottsdale at the age of 74.
He has 25 credited works on public record and has been recognised with Presidential Citizens Medal and Presidential Medal of Freedom.
The sections that follow break down Muhammad Ali's biography into quick facts, early life, career history, personal life and a year-by-year timeline.

sections.heading: Muhammad Ali — Early Life, Family and Education
paras: Muhammad Ali was born on 17 January 1942 in Louisville, and holds American nationality. He was given the name Cassius Marcellus Clay, Jr. at birth and is publicly known as Muhammad Ali.
Public records name his father, Cassius Marcellus Clay Sr. and his mother, Odessa Grady Clay. He is a sibling of Rahman Ali.
He studied at Santa Monica College and Central High School.
He is recorded as speaking English.

sections.heading: Muhammad Ali — Career and Professional Work
paras: Muhammad Ali works primarily as a boxer.
He has taken part in 1960 Summer Olympics.

sections.heading: Muhammad Ali — Family, Marriage and Personal Life
paras: He has been married to Sonji Roi (married 1964, until 1966), Khalilah Ali (married 1967, until 1977), Veronica Porché Ali (married 1977, until 1986) and Yolanda Williams (married 1986, until 2016).
He is a parent to Maryum Ali, Muhammad Ali Jr., Hana Ali, Laila Ali and Rasheda Ali.
He is associated with Scottsdale and Cherry Hill as a place of residence.
